guideTitle: The Best Docking Stations for Gaming Laptops, and What They Can't Do
breadcrumbLabel: Best Docking Stations for Gaming Laptops
metaTitle: Best Docking Stations for Gaming Laptops (2026)
metaDescription: Gaming laptops often need more power than a dock supplies and suffer on DisplayLink. We compared seven docks on refresh rate, display route, ports and charging.
introParagraphs: A dock can tidy a gaming laptop's desk, but two limits matter. Many gaming laptops draw more power under load than USB-C can supply, so keep the laptop's own charger connected while gaming. And DisplayLink docks, which drive displays in software, aren't suited to games.

For gaming on an external monitor, the most direct route is the laptop's own HDMI or DisplayPort. A dock is still useful for the rest of the setup, and a native high-refresh dock like the Razer USB4 Dock can drive fast monitors if your laptop has USB4 or Thunderbolt.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

razer-usb4-dock-14-port.summary: Razer's 14-port USB4 dock with dual monitors up to 4K at 120Hz, Ethernet, SD and audio.
razer-usb4-dock-14-port.description:
The Razer USB4 Dock is the one here designed around gaming: it drives two monitors at up to 4K 120Hz natively over USB4, which suits high-refresh displays, with 14 ports including HDMI, DisplayPort, Ethernet, SD and a 3.5mm jack.

It fast-charges a laptop and phone, but gaming laptops often need more power than USB-C provides under load, so keep the laptop's own charger connected while gaming. High-refresh output requires a USB4 or Thunderbolt port.
specs: Charging: laptop and phone fast charge
cons: Charging wattage not stated in summary
razer-usb4-dock-14-port.bestFor: USB4 gaming laptops with high-refresh monitors.
razer-usb4-dock-14-port.skipIf: Your laptop lacks USB4/Thunderbolt; a USB-C dock is the realistic option.

anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.badge: Triple Displays for Work, Not Games
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.summary: A 14-port DisplayLink dock with triple 4K at 60Hz, 140W output and a cooling fan.
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.description:
The Anker DL7400 drives three 4K displays at 60Hz via DisplayLink, with 140W output and a cooling fan. That suits a gaming laptop's work setup, but DisplayLink compresses video in software and isn't suited to games; connect your gaming monitor directly to the laptop.

It lists Windows laptops and requires the DisplayLink driver.
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.skipIf: You use a Mac; the Plugable UD-ULTCDL lists Mac support.

plugable-thunderbolt-4-100w.summary: A Thunderbolt 4 certified dock with 100W charging, dual 4K or single 6K output, SD and Ethernet.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-100w.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is the dock to choose if you want certified performance: it is Thunderbolt 4 certified, supports dual 4K or a single 6K display, and charges at up to 100W.

It has six USB ports, an SD card slot and Ethernet, needs no drivers on Mac or Windows, and Plugable lists it for M4 and M5 MacBook Air and Pro.

It was the most expensive dock here at the time of writing, and its full bandwidth needs a Thunderbolt or USB4 port on the laptop. Like every 100W dock, it won't match the charging speed of a larger laptop's higher-wattage charger.
cons: Most expensive here at the time of writing
Full bandwidth needs a Thunderbolt/USB4 port
plugable-thunderbolt-4-100w.bestFor: Thunderbolt and recent MacBook users who want dependable dual-display docking.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-100w.skipIf: You want high-refresh 4K; the Razer lists 4K at 120Hz.

wavlink-13-in-1-130w.summary: A DisplayLink dock with 130W PD rating, dual 5K/4K output, 2 HDMI, 2 DisplayPort and Ethernet.
wavlink-13-in-1-130w.description:
The WAVLINK uses DisplayLink to drive two external displays at up to 5K or 4K at 60Hz, which WAVLINK lists as working across M1 to M4 Macs and Windows. That matters because many base M-series Macs natively support only one external display.

It has a 130W PD rating, two HDMI and two DisplayPort outputs, Gigabit Ethernet, five USB ports and audio.

DisplayLink requires driver software, adds some processor load and is less suited to color-critical work or gaming. Charging to one laptop is still subject to USB PD limits.
pros: Dual displays on Macs that support only one natively
wavlink-13-in-1-130w.bestFor: Base M-series MacBooks that need two external monitors.
wavlink-13-in-1-130w.skipIf: Your laptop supports multiple displays natively; the Anker Nano avoids DisplayLink for less.

tobenone-18-in-1-150w.summary: An 18-in-1 dock with triple 4K via HDMI/DP/USB-C, 8 USB ports up to 10Gbps and a 150W adapter.
tobenone-18-in-1-150w.description:
The TobenONE 18-in-1 offers the most ports here: eight USB ports up to 10Gbps, triple 4K output across HDMI, DisplayPort and USB-C, and a 150W adapter with a 20W fast-charge port. It lists Windows and ChromeOS compatibility.

The listing summary doesn't confirm 2.5GbE, so check the Ethernet speed.
tobenone-18-in-1-150w.bestFor: Windows or Chromebook desks needing many ports.
tobenone-18-in-1-150w.skipIf: You want high-refresh output; the Razer is designed for it.

mokin-triple-4k-smart-display-gaming.summary: A triple-display USB-C dock with 3 HDMI and 2 DP, 100W, 10Gbps USB, Ethernet and a status display.
mokin-triple-4k-smart-display-gaming.description:
The MOKiN offers triple display output across three HDMI and two DisplayPort connections, with 100W charging, 10Gbps USB-A/C, Gigabit Ethernet and a small status display, at under $80 at the time of writing.

The listing summary doesn't say how the three displays are driven or at what refresh rate; triple display depends on your laptop.
mokin-triple-4k-smart-display-gaming.skipIf: You want high-refresh gaming output; connect the monitor to the laptop or use the Razer.

selore-triple-4k-100w-gaming.summary: A triple-4K USB-C dock with 3 HDMI and 2 DP, 100W, Ethernet, SD/microSD and a status display.
selore-triple-4k-100w-gaming.description:
The Selore closely matches the MOKiN's outputs, triple 4K across three HDMI and two DisplayPort, 100W, 10Gbps USB and Gigabit Ethernet, and adds an SD/microSD reader, at the lowest price here.

As with the MOKiN, the listing doesn't detail how the displays are driven or their refresh rate.
selore-triple-4k-100w-gaming.bestFor: Budget multi-monitor setups that also need a card reader.
selore-triple-4k-100w-gaming.skipIf: You need high refresh; the Razer lists 4K at 120Hz.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Use a native dock (Razer, Plugable) or the laptop's own port; avoid DisplayLink for games.
USB-C charging tops out at 100W for most docks; many gaming laptops need their own charger under load.
The Razer lists 4K at 120Hz; most others list 60Hz or don't say.
USB4/Thunderbolt docks need a matching laptop port.

faq.q: Can a dock power my gaming laptop?
faq.a: Often not fully under load; keep the laptop's own charger connected while gaming.
It isn't recommended; use native output or the laptop's own port.
The Razer lists dual monitors up to 4K at 120Hz.

faq.q: Do I need USB4 or Thunderbolt?
faq.a: For the Razer and Plugable at full capability, yes.
For work across three screens, yes; for gaming, connect the main monitor natively.

bottomLine: For gaming, the Razer USB4 Dock is the one designed for high-refresh monitors, if your laptop has USB4 or Thunderbolt; the Plugable TBT-UDM is the certified Thunderbolt 4 alternative.
The DisplayLink and budget triple-display docks suit work setups; for games, connect the monitor to the laptop directly and keep its own charger plugged in.
